## Summary
- The document explains the EU’s Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Act (IMERA), setting out how the single market should react to future crises.
- It introduces a permanent “resilience mechanism” to spot supply-chain risks and coordinate EU-wide responses before shortages become critical.
- Key tools include a new EU alert system, shared stockpiles of vital goods, and clearer rules for companies to keep production running during disruptions.
- The Act aims to reduce over-reliance on any single country for critical products like medicines, chips or batteries.
- It gives the European Commission stronger powers to gather data from firms and, if needed, impose temporary production orders.
- The two factsheets translate these rules into practical steps for policymakers and for business leaders.

## How this is useful to you
If you are lobbying on trade remedies or supply-chain security, use the factsheets to identify which sectors will face mandatory reporting and where the Commission can intervene first. They also flag the new alert thresholds that could trigger export bans or re-routing of goods, letting you brief clients on likely pinch-points before decisions are made.
